objectives.description: Add a doc_id -> provenance_fidelity lookup against $LITERATURE_DIR/index.json, fail-open on missing field
do_search: enrich each result object with a provenance_fidelity key
do_search: exclude unverified_summary/unverified_no_baseline from default ranking; add --include-unverified flag
do_read: prefix content with warning banner when provenance_fidelity != verified_conversion
do_read/do_toc result objects gain the provenance_fidelity key
Preserve existing behavior for verified_conversion docs
objectives.note: Verified live: blackburn_2002/doets_1987 chunks return unbannered content with provenance_fidelity=verified_conversion and normal ranking.

approaches_tried.approach: keyed the doc_id->provenance_fidelity map by index.json's .id (with a .parent_doc fallback for phantom-parent docs)
approaches_tried.reason: Live testing against .literature.db (blackburn_2002, doets_1987, thomason_1984 chunks) revealed that chunks_data.doc_id / chunks.json's doc_id is ALWAYS the bare source directory name, a namespace independent of index.json's .id field (blackburn_2002's index.json id is 'blackburn_2002_book', not 'blackburn_2002'). An .id-keyed map silently fail-opened (returned unverified_summary) for every already-chunked document whose id differs from its directory name -- i.e. most of the corpus.

approaches_tried.approach: keyed the doc_id->provenance_fidelity map by directory name, derived by stripping the 'sources/' prefix from each stamped entry's .path field
approaches_tried.reason: Matches chunks_data.doc_id exactly for every tested case (blackburn_2002, doets_1987, thomason_1984, venema_1991). Also transparently subsumes the old id/parent_doc fallback logic, since child entries' .path values resolve to the same directory-name key as any true-root entry in the same directory -- no separate phantom-parent-fallback branch needed on the retrieval side.

approaches_tried.approach: backtick-quoted inline code spans (e.g. `.id`/`.parent_doc`) inside Python docstrings/comments within unquoted bash heredocs (<< PYEOF, not << 'PYEOF')
approaches_tried.reason: Bash performs command substitution on backtick pairs anywhere in an unquoted heredoc body, including inside Python comments/docstrings, before python3 ever sees the text. Produced 'line N: .id: command not found' / '.parent_doc: command not found' shell errors at do_read invocation. Fixed by removing all backticks from comments inside these heredocs (plain-text field names instead, e.g. 'id/parent_doc fields').

deviations.description: 'Add a doc_id -> provenance_fidelity lookup ... mirroring get_project_doc_ids() (jq keyed by .id)'
deviations.reason: Implemented as a Python-embedded loader (one index.json parse per do_search/do_read/do_toc invocation, building an in-memory dict) rather than a separate bash+jq function called per result row. Same query pattern and fail-open semantics as get_project_doc_ids(), but avoids N per-row subprocess spawns since do_search/do_read/do_toc already run inside Python heredocs. Also implements the two-tier id-then-parent_doc fallback resolution required by Phase 2's phantom-parent stamping (see phase-2-progress.json deviation 2.5) — a plain get_project_doc_ids()-style single .id match would miss doets_1987/venema_1991/etc.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — python dict lookup with id-then-parent_doc fallback, in place of a bash+jq get_project_doc_ids()-style function)*
